# Incident Report — PCAP `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap`

No IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence directory — only the pcap. All findings below are derived directly from packet analysis.

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.17.215 | Top talker in all suspicious conversations |
| MAC | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.1.17.215` |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ | NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` records, DHCP option 12, matches `bluemoontuesday.com` AD domain |
| Logged-in user | shutchenson | Kerberos `CNameString` from 10.1.17.215 and DC 10.1.17.2 |

## Malware Family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS export was provided). The traffic matches the **"ClickFix" fake-CAPTCHA/verification lure technique**, which tricks the user into pasting and running an attacker-supplied command, leading to a commodity PowerShell backdoor and abuse of TeamViewer for hands-on-keyboard remote access. No YARA/ET signature is available in this evidence set to name a specific branded family with certainty.

**Delivery chain observed:**
1. `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (Cloudflare-fronted, 104.21.x.x) — fake "Google Authenticator/verify you're human" lure page.
2. Redirects to `authenticatoor.org` → 82.221.136.26:443, a known ClickFix-style CAPTCHA-lure host (TLS SNI observed).
3. Victim executes attacker command → downloads `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`, a VBScript/HTA "component" that spawns `powershell -WindowStyle Hidden` in the background while opening a decoy `https://azure.microsoft.com` tab, and pulls stage 2 from the same host.
4. Stage 2 (`29842.ps1` / `pas.ps1`, identical payload) is a Base64/obfuscated loader that computes the C: drive volume serial number as a bot ID and loops forever `DownloadString`-ing and `Invoke-Expression`-ing commands from `http://5.252.153.241/<serial>` every ~5.2 seconds — this beacon ran for the entire ~3200s capture.
5. Operator commands returned over that channel included `RunRH` ("PS process started") and a "startup shortcut created" persistence message, followed by delivery of `TeamViewer`, `TV`, and `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` from the same C2 IP — installing TeamViewer as a remote-access tool.
6. A large, sustained TLS session to 45.125.66.32:2917 (10MB down/587KB up over 1720s, TLS SNI = bare IP) immediately follows the TeamViewer install and is consistent with the attacker's live remote-control/relay session.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — primary backdoor C2; served the dropper, PowerShell payload, and TeamViewer components; received continuous `GET /1517096937` beacons (disk-serial bot ID) for the whole capture.
- `45.125.66.32:2917` — sustained TLS session with bare-IP SNI, high byte volume, following the TeamViewer install; behaviorally consistent with attacker remote-access/relay traffic.

**Domains**
- `authenticatoor.org` (→ 82.221.136.26) — ClickFix lure/landing page, DNS + TLS SNI observed.
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (→ 104.21.64.1 et al., Cloudflare) — fake verification page preceding the ClickFix domain.
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (→ 217.70.186.109) — queried immediately after the ClickFix chain; likely related redirect/lure infrastructure, lower confidence.

**URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — VBScript dropper.
- `http://5.252.153.241:80/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell backdoor (hardcoded inside the 264872 script).
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — same backdoor payload, fetched separately.
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`, `/TV`, `/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — TeamViewer RAT components.
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (and `?k=...` variants) — C2 beacon/check-in URL, `1517096937` is the victim's disk serial number in decimal.

**Files transferred (SHA256)**
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| 264872 (VBScript dropper) | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 |
| 29842.ps1 (PS backdoor) | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded |
| pas.ps1 (PS backdoor, dup) | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| TeamViewer | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e |
| TV | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 |

## Benign Context (not indicators)
Windows Update / Delivery Optimization (23.53.127.170, 199.232.214.172, 217.20.51.20), MS telemetry/NCSI (23.220.102.9, 23.205.110.x), Bing/MSN/Office (204.79.197.x, 13.107.x.x), NTP pool servers, legitimate TeamViewer master server `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26, standard DynGate protocol), NVIDIA GFE, LivePerson/Adobe/Yahoo analytics beacons, LinkedIn/Facebook trackers, LLMNR/mDNS/SSDP/NBNS local broadcast chatter, and the internal AD domain `bluemoontuesday.com` (DC at 10.1.17.2).

## Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74), logged in as user shutchenson, was compromised via a ClickFix-style fake verification lure (google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net → authenticatoor.org) that tricked the user into running an attacker command. This pulled a VBScript dropper and a persistent PowerShell backdoor from 5.252.153.241, which beaconed continuously using the host's disk serial number as an ID and used that channel to install TeamViewer for follow-on hands-on-keyboard remote access, evidenced by a large sustained session to 45.125.66.32:2917.
